reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 the end program header is exactly END PROGRAM program-name followed by a separator period, program-name a user-defined word identical to the name of a preceding PROGRAM-ID; the compiler must accept that form (for a separately compiled program and, via X.2.5, a contained one) and refuse a missing name, a missing period, a literal name, a mismatched name and the END FUNCTION keyword COBOL-85 does not have.

edition-consulted.switches: only the rule cited in the COBOL2793 / SR1 message (§1985:X.2.5.3 or X.2.5.4 at 85, §2023:10.7.3 later)
only the rule cited in COBOL2274 (§1985:X.2.5.4 GR2 vs §2023:10.6.1); END FUNCTION closing a PROGRAM-ID is refused by the same format test at every edition
Year >= 2002: where contained programs stand relative to the procedure division; not the header's own form

reader.edition-search: grep of EndMarkerPass.cs, SourceUnitShape.cs and the endProgramHeader / programName grammar rules for Edition|Year|CiteRule|ConstructRegistry
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the header's form and name rule run the same code; only diagnostic citations differ (a literal name is refused at 85 and at 2023 alike, COBOL5506)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise END PROGRAM on nested and sequenced programs and the END FUNCTION refusal; a missing period, a missing name, a literal name and a lowercase name are not exercised there

probes.expected: refused: COBOL-85 has only END PROGRAM

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.2.4.2  the text is in the clause or rule: "END PROGRAM program-name"
OK  §1985:VI.2.4.3 SR2  the text is in the clause or rule: "must be identical to a program-name declared in a preceding PROGRAM-ID paragraph"

reader.notes: The grammar rule endProgramHeader admits END (PROGRAM|FUNCTION) programName DOT; programName is a word only, so a literal is a parse refusal. SourceUnitShape refuses END FUNCTION on a PROGRAM-ID unit and EndMarkerPass refuses a mismatched name, citing the 1985 rules at --std 85.
